items: UTI was set up in 1963 under RBI initiative, but full regulatory control over all mutual funds was given to SEBI under the 1996 Regulations.
AMCs manage the fund portfolios, Trustees hold legal ownership of assets on behalf of investors, and Custodians hold securities in safe custody.
Frequently asked distinction: Open-ended funds permit continuous entry/exit at NAV, whereas Close-ended funds trade on stock exchanges with a fixed maturity.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: SEBI was established as a statutory body on January 30, 1992, under the SEBI Act, 1992, to protect investor interests and regulate securities markets.
Unit Trust of India (UTI), established in 1963 by an Act of Parliament, was the first mutual fund in India.
Mutual funds in India are structured as a three-tier system comprising the Sponsor, Public Trust (Trustees), and Asset Management Company (AMC).
SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996 provide the comprehensive regulatory framework for all mutual funds operating in India.
Net Asset Value (NAV) represents the market value per unit of a mutual fund scheme and is calculated on a daily basis.
